constraint_a: Format your response as a bulleted list using '-' for each point.
constraint_b: Please format your response as a numbered list using '1.', '2.', etc.

verifier.description: Counts top-level bullet markers (^- ) and numbered markers (^(\d+)[.)]) and classifies by which count is higher. Bullets nested under numbered headings are attributed to the numbered structure, not counted as standalone bullets.

root_causes.description: Degenerate single-character response '1' — model truncation/failure, not a verifier error. The response is too short to constitute any list format.

recommended_action: None — verifier is accurate, no issues found. The single baseline anomaly is a degenerate model output ('1'), not a verifier defect.

rubric.text: Classify as followed_a if the response is formatted as a bulleted list using dash markers ('- ') as the primary organizational structure. Classify as followed_b if the response is formatted as a numbered list using sequential numeric markers ('1.', '2.', etc.) as the primary organizational structure. When a response uses numbered headings with bullet sub-items underneath, classify as followed_b since the primary structure is numbered. Classify as followed_neither if the response contains no list formatting, uses a different marker style (e.g., asterisks, letters), or is a degenerate/empty response.

notes: This model produces exceptionally clean list formatting with zero ambiguity. Every condition C response uses exactly one format type — no mixed-format responses were found across all 2499 records.
The complement analysis (verify_a x verify_b matrix) shows perfect separation: 1351 bullets-only, 1148 numbered-only, 0 both, 0 neither.
Zero meta-commentary detected. The model never discusses the formatting instructions, it simply complies with one.
The single baseline anomaly (SBR(b) = 0.9796) is caused by a degenerate response consisting solely of the character '1', which is a model output failure, not a verifier limitation.

Directional asymmetry: system compliance is higher in a_to_b (77.3%) than b_to_a (69.2%), suggesting the model slightly favors bullets when system says bullets vs numbered when system says numbered. This is a behavioral observation, not a verifier issue.
